title: Merrick Western Edge near Rockville Centre
summary: Merrick community geography is described as extending west toward the Rockville Centre area, where Merrick, Rockaway, and other south shore Native histories met across waterways, meadows, and travel routes.
address_label: Rockville Centre / western Merrick homeland edge
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as a western-edge learning point for Merrick community geography.
why_this_matters: The Rockville Centre edge of Merrick country shows how Native homelands crossed the lines later drawn by towns, villages, and roads. It also helps explain why Merrick, Rockaway, and Massapequa histories often appear together in colonial records and local memory.
introduction_title: A Western Edge of Merrick Country
introduction_content:
Merrick territorial descriptions place Merrick communities on the southern part of Long Island from near Rockville Centre eastward toward Oyster Bay. That western edge was not a hard modern boundary; it was a lived south shore landscape of neighboring Native communities, waterways, meadows, and movement.

Merrick ancestral land is best understood as regional Native geography, not a single town boundary.
